questions.question: What significant event happened on Vaisakhi in 1699?

options.text: Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born
The first Sikh temple was built
Guru Gobind Singh Ji initiated the Khalsa

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Gobind Singh Ji initiated the Khalsa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On the day of **Vaisakhi** in **1699**, the tenth Sikh Guru, **Guru Gobind Singh Ji**, convened a massive assembly at **Anandpur Sahib** in Punjab to strengthen the Sikh faith against oppression.
 
• The Guru called for volunteers to sacrifice their lives, resulting in the selection of the **Panj Pyare** (the Five Beloved Ones), who were the first to be initiated into the **Khalsa Panth**.
 
• The initiation involved the **Amrit Sanchar** ceremony, where **Amrit** (holy nectar) was prepared in a steel bowl using a **Khanda** (double-edged sword) and administered to the devotees.
 
• This event formalised the Sikh identity by introducing the **Five Ks**, which every initiated Sikh must wear as symbols of their commitment and faith.
 
• The creation of the **Khalsa** aimed to establish a community of **Saint-Soldiers** who would uphold **Dharma**, promote social equality, and fight against the tyranny of the **Mughal Empire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Context of Other Options**:

 
 
• **Guru Nanak Dev Ji**: The founder of **Sikhism** was born in **1469** in **Nankana Sahib**, which occurred over 200 years prior to the 1699 **Vaisakhi** event.
 
• **The First Sikh Temple**: Historically, the first **Gurdwara** was established by **Guru Nanak Dev Ji** in **Kartarpur** around **1521**.
 
• **The Quran**: The central scripture of **Islam** was revealed to Prophet **Muhammad** starting in **610 AD** in the cave of **Hira**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Titles**:
 
 
• Following the initiation, the Guru gave the name **Singh** (Lion) to men and **Kaur** (Princess) to women to eliminate caste hierarchies and foster **universal brotherhood**.
 
• The Guru himself received initiation from the **Panj Pyare**, reinforcing that the Guru and the **Khalsa** are one entity.

questions.question: When you lie down on sand instead of standing, the pressure on sand is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lesser**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the physical force exerted on an object per unit **Area**. It is mathematically represented as **Pressure = Force / Area**.
 
• When a person is on sand, the **Force** acting downwards is the **Weight** of the person, which is calculated as the product of **Mass** and **Acceleration due to gravity (g)**. This force remains constant whether the person is standing or lying down.
 
• While **Standing**, the contact area between the body and the sand is limited to the soles of the **Feet**. This **Small Area** results in a high concentration of force, leading to **Higher Pressure**.
 
• While **Lying Down**, the body weight is distributed over a significantly **Larger Area** (the entire back or front of the body).
 
• According to the principle of **Inverse Proportion**, for a constant force, as the area of contact increases, the pressure exerted **Decreases**.
 
• Therefore, because the area of contact is much larger when lying down compared to standing, the pressure exerted on the sand is **Lesser**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The standard **SI Unit** of pressure is the **Pascal (Pa)**, where 1 Pa = 1 **Newton per square meter (N/m²)**.
 
• Understanding the relationship between area and pressure is vital in various engineering and biological contexts:
 
 
• **Foundation of Buildings**: Wide bases are used for pillars and walls to reduce the pressure on the ground, ensuring the structure does not sink.
 
• **Camel's Feet**: Camels have broad, padded feet that increase the **Surface Area** in contact with the desert sand, allowing them to exert **Lesser Pressure** and walk easily without sinking.
 
• **Tools**: Cutting tools like **Knives** and **Needles** have extremely small contact areas (sharp edges) to exert **High Pressure** with minimal force.

questions.question: The Meghalaya Plateau is an extension of which larger landform?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Peninsular Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Meghalaya Plateau**, also known as the **Shillong Plateau**, is geologically an extension of the **Indian Peninsular Plateau**, which is one of the oldest and most stable landmasses on Earth.
 
• It is separated from the main **Peninsular block** (specifically the **Chotanagpur Plateau**) by a massive tectonic depression known as the **Malda Fault** or the **Garo-Rajmahal Gap**.
 
• This gap was created due to the intense **down-faulting** caused by the northeastward movement of the **Indian Plate** during the **Himalayan orogeny**, which was later filled by the sediments of the **Ganga** and **Brahmaputra** rivers.
 
• The plateau comprises three distinct hill ranges named after the indigenous tribes: the **Garo Hills** in the west, the **Khasi Hills** in the center, and the **Jaintia Hills** in the east.
 
• The region is composed of **Archean** and **Pre-Cambrian** rocks, including **gneisses**, **granites**, and **schists**, which are identical to the rock structures found in the **Peninsular shield**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deccan Plateau**:

 
 
• A large **triangular plateau** located south of the **Narmada River**.
 
• It is primarily composed of **basaltic rocks** of volcanic origin, known as the **Deccan Traps**.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats**:
 
 
• A continuous mountain range running parallel to the **western coast** of India.
 
• It serves as the western boundary of the **Deccan Plateau** and is a global **biodiversity hotspot**.
 
 
 
• **Chotanagpur Plateau**:
 
 
• Located in eastern India, covering most of **Jharkhand** and parts of **West Bengal**, **Odisha**, and **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• Known as the **mineral heartland** of India, it is famous for its **Pat lands** and rich deposits of **coal** and **iron ore**.

questions.question: Why are the 1991 reforms sometimes linked to "jobless growth"?

options.text: Rising share of employment in agriculture
High GDP growth without proportionate employment expansion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High GDP growth without proportionate employment expansion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **jobless growth** refers to an economic phenomenon where a country experiences a significant increase in its **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** without a corresponding increase in **employment opportunities**.
 
• Following the **1991 Economic Reforms** (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization), India witnessed a shift from a **state-led** to a **market-led** economy, resulting in rapid growth in high-value sectors.
 
• The growth was predominantly driven by **capital-intensive** industries and the **Service Sector** (such as IT and Finance), which utilize advanced technology to increase productivity rather than relying on a large manual workforce.
 
• While the **aggregate output** of the economy expanded significantly, the **employment elasticity**—which measures how employment responds to GDP growth—declined, leading to a situation where wealth increased but the **unemployment rate** did not decrease proportionately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Employment Elasticity**:

 
 
• This economic indicator reflects the ability of an economy to generate jobs for every unit of **GDP growth**. Post-1991, this ratio fell sharply in India, particularly in the **secondary** and **tertiary** sectors.
 
 
 
• **Sectoral Mismatch**:
 
 
• The **Agriculture sector** continues to employ nearly half of the Indian workforce despite its shrinking contribution to the **total GDP**, leading to high levels of **disguised unemployment**.
 
• The **Manufacturing sector**, which traditionally absorbs low-skilled labor in developing economies, did not grow fast enough to accommodate the labor force exiting agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Skill Gap**:
 
 
• The post-reform growth favored **highly skilled professionals**, creating a **skill-biased technological change** that left many semi-skilled and unskilled workers in the **informal sector** with low wages and no job security.

questions.question: Chabahar Port is strategically positioned at the crossroads of which three regions?

options.text: East Asia, South Asia, and Africa
South Asia, Central Asia, and the Middle East
Europe, Central Asia, and East Asia
South America, Africa, and South Asia

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South Asia, Central Asia, and the Middle East**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chabahar Port** is located on the **Makran Coast** of the **Sistan and Baluchestan Province** in southeastern **Iran**, situated along the **Gulf of Oman**.
 
• The port acts as a primary maritime gateway for **South Asia**, specifically providing **India** with a strategic trade route that bypasses land boundaries to access **Afghanistan** and beyond.
 
• It serves as a critical transit hub for **Central Asia**, offering landlocked nations such as **Uzbekistan**, **Turkmenistan**, and **Kazakhstan** essential access to the **Indian Ocean** and global shipping lanes.
 
• As a major infrastructure project within **Iran**, it facilitates economic integration across the **Middle East** (West Asia) by connecting the **Arabian Sea** with the **Caspian Sea** region through internal rail and road networks.
 
• The strategic positioning of the port at these crossroads makes it a cornerstone of the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**, aimed at reducing transit time and freight costs between **India**, **Russia**, and **Europe**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminal Infrastructure**:

 
 
• The port consists of two main terminals: **Shahid Beheshti** and **Shahid Kalantari**. India has been actively involved in developing the **Shahid Beheshti** terminal to enhance regional connectivity.
 
• It is the only Iranian port with direct access to the **ocean**, allowing it to handle large cargo vessels that cannot enter the shallower **Persian Gulf**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Agreements**:
 
 
• The **Trilateral Transit Agreement** signed between **India**, **Iran**, and **Afghanistan** in **2016** established a dedicated corridor for the movement of goods and passengers.
 
• It supports the **Ashgabat Agreement**, which is an international transport and transit corridor facilitating trade between **Central Asia** and the **Persian Gulf**.
 
• The development of the **Chabahar-Zahedan railway** is intended to further link the port to the **Zaranj-Delaram road** in **Afghanistan**, boosting regional stability and commerce.

questions.question: Which crop has the strongest agro-ecological association with the black soil (regur) tracts of India?

options.text: Tea cultivation in acidic hill soils

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cotton cultivation in regur basins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Regur soil**, popularly known as **Black Cotton Soil**, is predominantly found in the **Deccan Trap** region of India, covering approximately **5.46 lakh sq km**.
 
• This soil is formed by the weathering of **basaltic lava rocks** from the **Cretaceous period**, making it rich in minerals like **iron**, **magnesium**, and **aluminum**.
 
• It possesses a very high **clay content** (often 60% or more), which gives it a superior **moisture-retention capacity**, a critical factor for the **Cotton** crop that requires consistent hydration during its growth cycle.
 
• Geographical concentration is highest in states like **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and parts of **Karnataka** and **Telangana**.
 
• The soil exhibits a unique **swell-shrink** property due to the presence of **Montmorillonite** clay; it swells when wet and develops deep cracks when dry, facilitating **self-aeration** or **self-ploughing**.
 
• The agro-ecological association is so strong that the presence of **regur soil** is the primary determinant for the location of **textile industries** in western India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jute cultivation in alluvial floodplains**

 
 
• **Jute** (the Golden Fibre) requires the fertile, renewable **silt** provided by **alluvial floodplains**, mainly in the **Ganges-Brahmaputra delta** (West Bengal and Bihar).
 
 
 
• **Tea cultivation in acidic hill soils**
 
 
• **Tea** thrives in **deep, fertile, and well-drained acidic soils** (pH 4.5 to 5.5) rich in organic matter, typically found in **Assam**, **Darjeeling**, and the **Nilgiri Hills**.
 
 
 
• **Rice cultivation in deltaic alluvium**
 
 
• **Rice** (Paddy) necessitates heavy **clayey alluvium** found in coastal **deltas** (like those of the **Godavari** and **Mahanadi**) because it requires soil that can hold standing water for long periods.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Cotton cultivation in regur basins**

questions.question: Which ministry launched the Nyaya Shruti App in August 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Home Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nyaya Shruti App** was officially launched in **August 2024** by the Union Minister of Home Affairs and Cooperation, **Amit Shah**, during a high-level review meeting in **Chandigarh**.
 
• The application is designed to facilitate the seamless implementation of the three new criminal laws: **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**, **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, and **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)**.
 
• The primary objective of the **Nyaya Shruti** system is to enable **video conferencing** for judicial proceedings, allowing witnesses, medical experts, and police officials to provide testimony remotely from a secure environment.
 
• By integrating with the **Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS)**, the app ensures that digital evidence and statements are recorded efficiently, reducing the physical burden on the judiciary and law enforcement agencies.
 
• The launch marks a critical step towards **e-Forensics** and **e-Courts**, aiming to expedite the delivery of justice and minimize the backlog of cases in the Indian legal system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**:

 
 
• Replaces the colonial-era **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)**.
 
• Mandates the use of **technology** for various stages of investigation, including the recording of search and seizure operations via mobile phones or electronic devices.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Law and Justice**:
 
 
• While this ministry oversees the drafting of legislation and legal affairs, the operational rollout of technology for the **new criminal laws** and internal security is managed by the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Transformation**:
 
 
• The **Nyaya Shruti** app is a component of the broader **Digital India** mission, specifically targeting the **Criminal Justice System** to ensure transparency and accountability.

questions.question: Which court in November 2024 said that a sexual harassment case cannot be closed after a compromise is reached between the rival parties as such offences have serious impact on the society?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2024**, the **Supreme Court of India** ruled that a **sexual harassment case cannot be quashed merely because the accused and the complainant have reached a compromise**. 
 
• The Court observed that offences involving **sexual harassment, sexual assault, and crimes against children** are not purely private disputes and have a **serious impact on society**. 
 
• The judgment was delivered by a bench comprising **Justice C. T. Ravikumar** and **Justice P. V. Sanjay Kumar**. 
 
• The Court set aside an order of the **Rajasthan High Court**, which had earlier quashed an FIR against a school teacher accused of sexually harassing a minor girl after a compromise was reached with the victim's family. 
 
• The case involved provisions of the **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act**, highlighting the judiciary's commitment to protecting children from sexual crimes. 
 
• The Supreme Court emphasized that heinous offences affecting public interest cannot ordinarily be terminated through private settlements because such crimes are considered offences against society as a whole. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court of India**

 
 
• Established on **26 January 1950** under **Part V, Chapter IV** of the Constitution of India.
 
• It is the **highest judicial authority** in the country.
 
• The Court has the power of **judicial review** and acts as the final interpreter of the Constitution.
 
• Its decisions are binding on all courts within India under **Article 141** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Patna High Court**
 
 
• Established in **1916**.
 
• It is the highest judicial body for the state of **Bihar**.
 
• Its principal seat is located in **Patna**.
 
 
 
• **Madras High Court**
 
 
• One of India's oldest High Courts, established in **1862**.
 
• Exercises jurisdiction over the state of **Tamil Nadu** and the Union Territory of **Puducherry**.
 
• Its principal seat is located in **Chennai**.
 
 
 
• **POCSO Act, 2012**
 
 
• Enacted to protect children below **18 years of age** from sexual offences.
 
• Provides for child-friendly procedures during investigation and trial.
 
• Recognizes offences such as **sexual assault, aggravated sexual assault, sexual harassment, and use of children for pornography**.

questions.question: Which Chalukya ruler defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada River?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakesin II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The battle between **Harshavardhana** and **Pulakesin II** occurred on the banks of the **Narmada River** around **618-619 CE**.
 
• **Pulakesin II** belonged to the **Chalukyas of Vatapi** (Badami) and was one of the most powerful rulers of the **Deccan**.
 
• **Harshavardhana**, the ruler of **Kannauj**, attempted to expand his empire into southern India but was decisively checked by the **Chalukyan** forces.
 
• The **Aihole Inscription**, authored by the court poet **Ravikirti**, provides a detailed account of this victory and the valor of **Pulakesin II**.
 
• Following this victory, **Pulakesin II** assumed the title of **Paramesvara** and established the **Narmada River** as the permanent boundary between the two empires.
 
• The Chinese traveler **Xuanzang** (Hiuen Tsang), who visited the courts of both kings, also recorded the military strength of **Pulakesin II** and his success in resisting **Harsha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajendra I**:

 
 
• He was a preeminent ruler of the **Chola Dynasty** (1014−1044 CE).
 
• He is famous for his naval expeditions to **Southeast Asia** and his campaign to the **Ganga River**, after which he took the title **Gangaikonda**.
 
 
 
• **Krishna III**:
 
 
• He was the last great emperor of the **Rashtrakuta Dynasty** of **Manyakheta**.
 
• He defeated the **Cholas** at the **Battle of Takkolam** in **949 CE** and extended his influence as far as **Rameswaram**.
 
 
 
• **Rajasimha**:
 
 
• Also known as **Narasimhavarman II**, he was a notable ruler of the **Pallava Dynasty**.
 
• He is renowned for his patronage of **Dravidian architecture**, specifically the construction of the **Shore Temple** at **Mahabalipuram** and the **Kailasanathar Temple** at **Kanchipuram**.

questions.question: Uttarakhand is known for which of the following traditional folk dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**choliya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Choliya**, also known as **Chholiya**, is one of the oldest and most famous folk dances of the **Kumaon region** in **Uttarakhand**.
 
• It is traditionally a **sword dance** that dates back over a **thousand years**, reflecting the **martial traditions** of the **Khasa** and **Rajput** communities of the **Himalayan** belt.
 
• Originally performed at **wedding processions** to ward off evil spirits, the dance involves a mock combat sequence where dancers wield **swords** (talwar) and **shields** (dhala) with rhythmic precision.
 
• The performance is characterized by high-energy movements, **acrobatic stunts**, and synchronized formations that showcase the bravery and agility of the warriors.
 
• It is accompanied by traditional musical instruments of **Uttarakhand**, specifically the **Dhol**, **Damau**, **Turi**, **Ransingha**, and **Masakbeen** (bagpipes).
 
• Dancers typically wear traditional **Kumaoni** attire, consisting of white **chudidar pajamas**, a long **chola** (tunic), and a **turban**, often decorated with colorful embroidery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kolkali**:

 
 
• A rhythmic folk dance performed in the state of **Kerala** and the Union Territory of **Lakshadweep**.
 
• Dancers move in a circle, striking **wooden sticks** in unison to create a unique percussive sound.
 
 
 
• **Sambalpuri**:
 
 
• Originates from the **western region** of **Odisha**.
 
• It is often associated with the **Dalkhai** dance and is performed during festivals like **Nuakhai** and **Bhai Jiuntia**.
 
 
 
• **Sawlakin** (Sarlamkai):
 
 
• This is a prominent folk dance from the state of **Mizoram**.
 
• Historically, it was a **war dance** performed to celebrate a victory in battle and is also known as **Solakia** in some tribal dialects.
 
 
 
• Other Folk Dances of **Uttarakhand**:
 
 
• **Jhora**: A community dance performed during **Vasant Panchami**.
 
• **Chhapeli**: A romantic dance style representing the courtship between lovers.
 
• **Langvir Nritya**: An acrobatic dance performed by men involving climbing a pole.

questions.question: In 2025, Indian Railways has successfully tested the country's first hydrogen-powered coach in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chennai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In early **2025**, Indian Railways reached a major milestone in green transportation by successfully testing its first **hydrogen-powered coach** at the **Integral Coach Factory (ICF)** in **Chennai**.
 
• The coach is a part of the ambitious **Hydrogen for Heritage** initiative, which aims to replace carbon-heavy diesel engines with environment-friendly **hydrogen fuel cell** technology on historical and sensitive rail routes.
 
• Technologically, these coaches utilize **fuel cells** to combine hydrogen and oxygen to generate electricity, with the only emissions being **water vapor** and heat, making them a **zero-emission** alternative to traditional rolling stock.
 
• The successful prototype testing at **Chennai** facilitates the deployment of these trains on various narrow-gauge sections, such as the **Kalka-Shimla** and **Darjeeling Himalayan Railway**.
 
• This development aligns with India's national commitment to achieve **Net Zero Carbon Emission** by **2030** and reduces the dependence on imported fossil fuels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai**:

 
 
• Established in **1955**, it is the world's largest rail coach manufacturer and is renowned for designing the **Vande Bharat Express** (Train 18).
 
 
 
• **Rail Coach Factory (RCF), Kapurthala**:
 
 
• Located in **Punjab**, this unit was established in **1986** and is a primary manufacturer of **LHB (Linke Hofmann Busch)** coaches used in high-speed trains.
 
 
 
• **Modern Coach Factory (MCF), Rae Bareilly**:
 
 
• Commissioned in **2012** in **Uttar Pradesh**, it is a state-of-the-art facility focused on automated manufacturing of specialized railway coaches.
 
 
 
• **Kolkata**:
 
 
• It is the headquarters of the **Eastern Railway** and **South Eastern Railway**, and was the first city in India to launch a **Metro Railway** system in **1984**.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, which state recorded the highest rural population in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census 2011**, **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest **rural population** in India, with a total of **155,110,594** individuals living in rural areas.
 
• The state accounts for nearly **18.62%** of the total rural population of the country, which stood at approximately **833.7 million** during the 2011 survey.
 
• Approximately **77.73%** of the total population of **Uttar Pradesh** resides in rural regions, emphasizing its role as a primarily agrarian and rural-based economy.
 
• The **15th National Census** of India, conducted in two phases (House Listing and Population Enumeration), serves as the primary source for these **demographic statistics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with other states:
 
 
• **Bihar**: It holds the second-highest **rural population** in India, with approximately **92.3 million** people living in villages.
 
• **West Bengal**: This state ranks among the top contributors with a rural population of about **62.1 million**.
 
• **Maharashtra**: While it has the highest **urban population** in India (**50.8 million**), its rural population is approximately **61.5 million**.
 
 
 
• Key Census Facts:
 
 
• **Sikkim**: Recorded as the state with the **lowest total population** in India.

questions.solution:

• The **21st Asian Games** are scheduled to be hosted in **Doha, Qatar**, in the year **2030**.
 
• The decision was finalized during the **39th General Assembly** of the **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)**, which took place in **Muscat, Oman**, on **16 December 2020**.
 
• **Doha** was awarded the **2030** edition after winning the majority of votes in a contest against **Riyadh, Saudi Arabia**. As part of a consensus, the **OCA** subsequently awarded the **22nd Asian Games** to **Riyadh** for the year **2034**.
 
• This event marks the second time **Qatar** will host the continental multi-sport competition, having previously organized the **15th Asian Games** in **2006**.
 
• The **2030 Games** are expected to utilize many of the state-of-the-art venues developed for the **2022 FIFA World Cup**, demonstrating **Qatar**'s established sports infrastructure.

questions.question: Which organization publishes the Global Education Monitoring Report?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UNESCO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Report** is an editorially independent, authoritative, and evidence-based annual report published by **UNESCO**.
 
• The report is mandated to monitor progress towards the education targets in the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** framework, with a specific focus on **SDG 4**, which aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education.
 
• Originally established in **2002**, it was formerly known as the **Education for All (EFA) Global Monitoring Report** before being rebranded in **2016** following the adoption of the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**.
 
• Each edition of the report focuses on a specific theme, such as **inclusion and education**, **non-state actors**, or **technology in education**, providing a comprehensive assessment of global education trends and policy recommendations.
 
• It serves as a vital tool for **advocacy** and **accountability**, using the latest available data to hold governments and international organizations responsible for their educational commitments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization)**:

 
 
• Founded in **1945** and headquartered in **Paris, France**, its mission is to build peace through international cooperation in **Education**, the **Sciences**, and **Culture**.
 
 
 
• **UNDP (United Nations Development Programme)**:
 
 
• Headquartered in **New York**, it is primarily known for publishing the **Human Development Report (HDR)** and the **Human Development Index (HDI)**.
 
 
 
• **World Bank**:
 
 
• An international financial institution that provides loans and grants; it publishes the **World Development Report (WDR)** and the **Global Economic Prospects**.
 
 
 
• **WIPO (World Intellectual Property Organization)**:
 
 
• A specialized agency of the UN that promotes the protection of **intellectual property** and publishes the **Global Innovation Index (GII)**.
